correctness.rationale: For q=4 the cosine interaction is exactly the sum of two Ising interactions with coupling J/2. All single-component flips are available, and flipping both costs the sum, so weak blocking factors. Ising wall patterns are cyclic independent sets of even size; the two choices of initial spin cancel the factor 1/2 in the parity projection. The matrices at weights ±1 have the claimed eigenvalues. For q=5 each middle spin must maximize the projection on the sum of its neighbours: equal neighbours force their common spin, neighbouring colours permit either endpoint, and two-step neighbours force their short-arc midpoint. Thus in (0,+1,−1) coordinates only the two adjacent opposite nonzero increments are disallowed. Closure requires the increment sum to be zero mod 5, and the five initial spins cancel the character projection factor 1/5. The trace counts labelled cycles, not necklaces. No nontrivial twist attains the Perron radius: equality in the triangle inequality for a Perron-modulus eigenvector would force a common phase on all three self-loops, which is impossible. Both leading coefficients are one, giving the stated ratio. An independent spin-pair transfer with exact local scores in Z[sqrt(5)] was run for n=3..16 using /workspace/independent_checks/clock_local_scores.py; it gave the five reported small-n pairs and, for example, (4866436,1332585) at n=16. The finite run corroborates, rather than proves, the all-n formulas.
